jurisdiction: City of Goodlettsville voters only (the city's Sumner County voters see it on Sumner's ballot)
official_title: City of Goodlettsville Sales and Use Tax Referendum. Shall the Goodlettsville Investment Act (Ordinance No. 26-1146) for the purpose of investing in vital City services such as parks, roads, and public safety, by increasing the City’s sales tax by a half-penny per dollar, be approved?
plain_summary: Raises the sales tax in Goodlettsville by half a cent per dollar, 50 cents on every $100 spent. The city says the money would go to public safety, roads, sidewalks and parks.
yes_means: The sales tax in Goodlettsville goes up by half a cent per dollar.
no_means: Goodlettsville's sales tax stays where it is.
fiscal_impact: The city estimates about $3 million more a year. WSMV reports the rate on the Davidson County side of the city would become 10.25%, the highest in Tennessee, and 9.75% on the Sumner County side. The ordinance doesn't require the money to go to any particular project.
confusing_wording_note: You'll mark For or Against, not Yes or No. For means you approve the tax increase.

supporters_case.text: Goodlettsville's city manager, Julie High, told WSMV a sales tax is “shared by everyone who shops and dines in our city,” not only residents, and that costs for police and fire have grown faster than revenue.

opponents_case.text: We found no organized campaign or official argument on this side.

explainers.title: Goodlettsville referendum would create highest sales tax in Tennessee
Goodlettsville voters to decide on sales tax increase that would fund police, fire and park upgrades
